validity.recommendation: Keep the row (real, gas, 18-in confirmed). Update Status to operating (see status_reviews). Optionally note it is a dedicated power-plant feeder, not a trunk line.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: Real. The row's sole cited source is the Iraq Oil Ministry / State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP, 'شركة المشاريع النفطية') project-status PDF at opc-storage.oil.gov.iq dated 2025-05-20. Layout-preserving extraction (pdftotext -layout) of that PDF shows, as project row 11: 'عقد تنفيذ مد انبوب الغاز الجاف 18 عقدة المغذي لمحطة كهرباء كربلاء الغازية' = 'Contract for laying the 18(-in) dry-gas feeder pipe for the Karbala gas power station' (cost 4,000; planned 100%; actual completion 100%; deviation 0). Karbala appears three ways in the doc (rows 10, 11) so it is unambiguously named. Independently, GE Vernova's Feb-2025 press release lists Karbala among Iraqi plants that 'already transitioned from heavy fuel oil (HFO) to natural gas' (+~260 MW). Two independent origins (Oil Ministry pipe contractor + GE Vernova/Ministry of Electricity turbine program) => not a GEM-only phantom. CLASSIFICATION: Commodity gas is correct ('الغاز الجاف' = dry gas). PipelineType=transmission is defensible but note the source explicitly calls it a feeder ('المغذي') dedicated to one power plant, i.e. a lateral/supply line rather than a transmission trunk; minor caveat only. DUPLICATE: No duplicate within the 16-pipeline roster. The same SCOP table lists SEPARATE feeder pipes for the Hilla (24-in, row 12) and Taji (18-in, row 13) gas power stations, but neither is in the roster, so P7470 is uniquely the Karbala line. ATTRIBUTION: Owner = Iraq Ministry of Oil is correct (SCOP is the Oil Ministry's executing arm). Endpoint = Karbala province is correct (feeds محطة كهرباء كربلاء الغازية). StartLocation/gas source origin is not stated in the doc. SPEC: Diameter 18 in is CONFIRMED by row 11 of the source (an earlier char-reversed extraction wrongly suggested 24 in; the layout extraction resolves it to 18 in for Karbala, 24 in for Hilla). Length and Capacity are blank in GEM and the source gives neither (only cost in IQD-millions and % completion) — left blank, not fabricated.

fills.researcher_notes: No throughput/capacity figure found. The SCOP source gives only contract cost (4,000 IQD-mn) and % completion; GE Vernova gives a plant MW figure, not pipe capacity. Not fabricating a number.
No pipe length stated in the SCOP source or any independent source found. Left blank.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: GEM has Status=construction (LastUpdated 2025-07-22), but the sheet's OWN cited SCOP source (dated 2025-05-20) shows the Karbala dry-gas feeder execution contract (row 11) at 100% planned AND 100% actual completion, deviation 0 — i.e. the pipe is physically built. Independently, GE Vernova's Feb-2025 release lists Karbala among plants that have 'already transitioned from HFO to natural gas', implying the plant is receiving/burning gas. Together these two independent origins support the line being complete and in service, so 'operating' fits better than 'construction'. Caveat: neither source uses the word 'operating/commissioned' for the pipe itself and no exact in-service date is given, so tier=medium and StartYear1 set to 2025 (year both the plant conversion and the 100%-complete pipe are attested). If a reviewer prefers strict evidence of gas flow, the fallback is to keep construction but flag it as complete/awaiting commissioning. Verifier: OPC PDF returns 200 (contains '18'; Arabic Karbala token confirmed via pdftotext -layout row 11); GE Vernova PR 200 + contains 'Karbala'/'natural gas'.

summary: P7470 Karbla Gas Pipeline is real (18-in dry-gas feeder to Karbala gas power station, Oil Ministry/SCOP + GE Vernova); diameter 18 in confirmed; no duplicate; but Status=construction is stale — source shows the pipe 100% complete (May 2025) and plant on gas (Feb 2025), so proposing operating/StartYear1 2025.
